claim: For Llama 3 models, simple binary relational facts—triples of the form (subject, relation, object)— are localized in identifiable MLP weights and attention modules in intermediate layers that function as dedicated storage units for individual facts. Causal tracing and activation analysis can isolate these elements with sufficient precision to enable knowledge editing achieving high success rates on UniEdit benchmark (with both reliability and generality > 90%) while maintaining collateral effects below 5% as measured by impact to the model's performance on MMLU benchmark.
subclaims: For Llama 3 models, are simple binary relational facts localized in identifiable MLP weights?
For Llama 3 models, are simple binary relational facts localized in attention modules?
Are these MLP weights and attention modules located in intermediate layers?
Do these intermediate-layer components function as dedicated storage units for individual facts?
Can causal tracing isolate these fact-storing elements with sufficient precision?
Can activation analysis isolate these fact-storing elements with sufficient precision?
Does isolating these elements enable knowledge editing on the UniEdit benchmark?
Does this knowledge editing achieve reliability greater than 90% on the UniEdit benchmark?
Does this knowledge editing achieve generality greater than 90% on the UniEdit benchmark?
Does this knowledge editing maintain collateral effects below 5%?
Are collateral effects measured by impact on the model’s performance on the MMLU benchmark?
baseline_experiments: To address subclaims 1, 2, 3, 5, and 6, run a localization study on public Llama 3 checkpoints using simple binary relational facts from a public dataset such as CounterFact, zsRE, or the factual portions of UniEdit if publicly available. First verify that the model answers each fact correctly under multiple prompt templates. Then apply causal tracing: corrupt the subject-token representation, restore activations at individual layers/modules, and measure recovery of the correct object probability. Separately run activation analysis by collecting MLP and attention activations for true-fact prompts versus matched control prompts and ranking neurons, MLP channels, attention heads, and attention output projections by causal/activation importance. Compare whether high-importance components are concentrated in identifiable MLP weights, attention modules, and especially intermediate layers rather than early or late layers. Possible conclusions: if a small, reproducible set of intermediate-layer MLP and/or attention components restores object prediction across prompt variants, this supports localization and isolatability; if importance is diffuse, unstable across prompts, or concentrated outside intermediate layers, it weakens the localization and intermediate-layer subclaims. This experiment could be made partly unnecessary by prior public causal-tracing results specifically on Llama 3, with released prompts, checkpoints, component rankings, and ablation/patching code.

To address subclaim 4, test whether the localized intermediate-layer components function as dedicated storage units for individual facts rather than generic semantic or syntactic features. Using the components identified in Experiment 1, perform targeted ablations and patching for each fact and measure specificity on: the target fact, paraphrases of the same fact, facts sharing the same subject, facts sharing the same relation, facts sharing the same object, and unrelated facts, using public datasets such as CounterFact, zsRE, PopQA, and UniEdit. Also test many-to-one and one-to-many relations to see whether the same component stores multiple facts. Possible conclusions: if ablating a small component selectively disrupts one fact while preserving nearby and unrelated facts, and patching restores only that fact, this supports the dedicated-storage-unit interpretation; if the same component affects many related facts, broad concepts, or general language performance, the evidence would favor distributed or feature-level representation rather than individual fact storage. This experiment could be made unnecessary by a released specificity dataset and component-level ablation matrix showing one-to-one correspondence between Llama 3 components and individual relational facts.

To address subclaims 7, 8, 9, 10, and 11, implement a knowledge-editing pipeline that edits only the components isolated by causal tracing or activation analysis, then evaluate it on the public UniEdit benchmark and measure collateral effects with MMLU. For each requested edit, modify the identified MLP weights and/or attention parameters, then compute UniEdit reliability as success on direct edited prompts and generality as success on paraphrased or semantically equivalent prompts, using the benchmark’s standard metrics. Evaluate collateral effects by comparing pre-edit and post-edit Llama 3 accuracy on the public MMLU test/dev split or standard HuggingFace MMLU tasks, reporting the percentage-point drop and requiring it to remain below 5%. Include baselines such as ROME, MEMIT, LoRA fine-tuning, and random same-size component edits. Possible conclusions: reliability and generality both above 90% with MMLU degradation below 5%, significantly outperforming baselines or random edits, would support the editing-performance part of the claim; lower success, poor generality, or MMLU drops above 5% would refute or qualify it. This experiment could be made unnecessary by an independently reproducible UniEdit/MMLU report for Llama 3 with released edit lists, edited checkpoints or weight deltas, and exact evaluation scripts.
method_experiments: To address subclaims 1, 2, 3, 4, and 5, run a causal-tracing and causal-ablation localization study on Llama 3 8B and, if compute permits, Llama 3 70B using simple factual triples from public CounterFact, zsRE, and/or UniEdit factual-editing splits available on HuggingFace. For each triple prompt, measure the clean object-token logit, corrupt the subject representation or prompt, and then restore activations one module at a time at every layer, separately for MLP blocks and attention outputs/heads. Compute the indirect causal effect of each module on recovering the correct object. Then ablate or patch only the top-ranked MLP neurons/weight columns and attention heads and test whether the object prediction changes while unrelated facts remain stable. Analyze whether high-effect components are concentrated in intermediate layers rather than early or late layers, whether both MLPs and attention modules show significant effects, and whether the same components are specific to one fact or reused across many facts. If effects are sharply localized to a small number of intermediate-layer MLP weights and/or attention heads and ablating them selectively destroys the target fact with little impact on controls, this would support the localization and dedicated-storage subclaims. If effects are diffuse, mostly late-layer, prompt-dependent, or shared across many facts, it would weaken the claim. This experiment could be partly unnecessary if there already exists a public Llama 3 causal-tracing atlas showing per-fact MLP and attention localization with specificity tests across thousands of triples.

To address subclaims 4 and 6, perform an independent activation-analysis experiment to see whether fact-storing elements can be isolated without causal tracing. Use the same public factual triples and generate multiple paraphrased prompts per triple, plus negative controls sharing the same subject, relation, or object. Collect residual-stream, MLP, and attention-head activations across all layers of Llama 3. Fit sparse linear probes, sparse autoencoder features, or attribution-based classifiers to identify minimal activation dimensions, neurons, MLP channels, or attention heads that distinguish the correct object relation from controls. Validate precision by testing whether the identified elements generalize across paraphrases of the same fact but not to neighboring facts, and compare the resulting elements with those found by causal tracing in Experiment 1. If activation analysis isolates compact intermediate-layer components that overlap strongly with causal-tracing targets and are selective for individual triples, this supports the activation-analysis and dedicated-storage subclaims. If probes rely on broad distributed patterns, surface-form artifacts, or components that do not causally affect generation when patched or ablated, the claim is weakened. This experiment could be made unnecessary by stronger evidence consisting of publicly released Llama 3 activation-feature maps with causal validation and per-fact selectivity statistics.

To address subclaims 7, 8, 9, 10, and 11, run a targeted knowledge-editing benchmark using the elements isolated in Experiments 1 and 2. On the public UniEdit benchmark, edit Llama 3 by modifying only the identified MLP weights and/or attention modules for each requested triple update, and compare against baselines such as ROME, MEMIT, MEND, random intermediate-layer edits, and untargeted full-layer edits. Measure UniEdit reliability as success on the edited prompt, generality as success on paraphrases and equivalent prompts, and locality/collateral damage on unrelated UniEdit examples. Then evaluate the same pre-edit and post-edit models on the public MMLU benchmark and define collateral effect as relative or absolute degradation in MMLU accuracy, pre-registering the below-5% threshold. If targeted edits achieve reliability and generality above 90% while reducing MMLU performance by less than 5%, and outperform random or diffuse baselines, this supports the claim that isolated elements enable high-quality editing with low collateral effects. If reliability or generality falls below 90%, if MMLU drops by more than 5%, or if comparable performance is achieved by non-localized baselines, the editing portion of the claim is not supported. This experiment could be unnecessary if a reproducible public UniEdit leaderboard for Llama 3 already reports targeted MLP/attention edits with reliability, generality, and MMLU collateral-effect measurements under the same thresholds.
